meta.scene_summary: We are building an AI-optimized future while our current infrastructure is still struggling to stay online.

cooking.headline: Mistral just dropped Large 4, because being the best model in the world has the shelf life of milk.
cooking.summary: Mistral is back to prove that the state-of-the-art crown is just a rental property with a monthly lease. It's impressive how they keep updating the model, though I'm starting to think my GPU is actually just a space heater in disguise.
cooking.plain_english: Mistral has released a new version of its most powerful artificial intelligence model.

cooking.headline: Polars 2.0 is here, and it's basically the library equivalent of hitting the gym.
cooking.summary: Polars 2.0 has arrived to make your dataframes move even faster, because apparently, waiting five seconds for a CSV to load was far too much to ask. It's the perfect upgrade for when your code needs to stop acting like a sluggish group project partner and actually get the job done.
cooking.plain_english: The Polars data processing library has released a new major version that includes performance improvements and architectural changes.

cooking.headline: AI is now designing its own hardware, because humans were clearly the bottleneck.
cooking.summary: We've reached the point where AI is designing its own inference chips, effectively cutting out the middleman in the hardware supply chain. It's like the AI version of a student writing their own final exam just to make sure they pass with flying colors.
cooking.plain_english: Researchers have developed an artificial intelligence system capable of designing custom hardware for processing AI models.

cooking.headline: AI agents are now doing the hard science homework for us
cooking.summary: Opus 5.5 just discovered new magnetic semiconductor candidates, which is essentially the AI version of a junior dev actually solving a ticket on the first try. It's great news for physics, but now I'm worried that my coffee machine is going to start filing patents while I'm still struggling to wake up.
cooking.plain_english: An artificial intelligence system has identified two potential materials that could improve the efficiency of electronic devices at room temperature.

cooking.headline: Geothermal energy just speedran its construction phase
cooking.summary: Building a power plant in under two years is basically the infrastructure equivalent of finishing a project before the deadline without a single emergency meeting. It turns out that when you stop hitting bureaucratic walls, you can actually get things done in this decade.
cooking.plain_english: A new geothermal energy facility was successfully built and completed in 23 months.

cooking.headline: Transformers just learned to skip the math homework
cooking.summary: Researchers found a way to train massive models without backpropagation, which is the machine learning equivalent of passing a final exam without ever opening the textbook. It turns out you don't actually need the most tedious part of the process to get the right answer.
cooking.plain_english: A new research method allows artificial intelligence models to be trained without using the standard backpropagation algorithm.

cooking.headline: A datalake that actually drinks from the firehose
cooking.summary: Parseable claims it can ingest 100 million time-series data points per minute, which is perfect for when your microservices decide to have a collective mental breakdown all at once. It's nice to have a place to store the logs while you pretend you know why the server is on fire.
cooking.plain_english: Parseable is a new software platform designed to store and analyze large volumes of time-series data at high speeds.

cooked.headline: JetBrains lost money for the first time, proving that even the best IDEs can't debug a bad balance sheet.
cooked.summary: The company that powers half our daily productivity has finally hit a red quarter. It's ironic that the people who built the tools to optimize our workflows are now struggling to optimize their own bottom line.
cooked.plain_english: The software development company JetBrains reported its first financial loss since it began tracking its performance.

cooked.headline: GitHub Actions decided to take an unscheduled weekend off
cooked.summary: GitHub's automation engine went down, proving that your entire CI/CD pipeline is just a house of cards waiting for a breeze. It's the developer equivalent of showing up to the office only to find the building locked and the lights off.
cooked.plain_english: GitHub experienced a service outage that prevented users from running automated software workflows.

cooked.headline: ASOS push notifications are now a chaotic group chat with hackers
cooked.summary: ASOS users started getting random push notifications from hackers instead of sale alerts, turning a shopping app into a security disaster. Nothing says 'great user experience' like your favorite clothing store sending you unauthorized messages from the void.
cooked.plain_english: Unauthorized individuals gained access to the ASOS push notification system and sent messages to the app's users.
